x-notes: Seed objects reference each other with the `@ref:<slug>` token (`@ref:<Schema>:<slug>` when a slug is not unique), NEVER with a bare slug. OpenRegister's ImportHandler::resolveSeedReferenceTokens() runs before the import loop: it mints or reuses a stable UUID for every referenced target, writes it into that target's `@self.id`, and replaces the tokens with that UUID -- so the relation properties (`$ref` + `format: uuid`) see a real UUID by the time saveObject() validates. A bare slug fails that validation and the whole seed object is DROPPED with only a log line, which is how 103 of 107 references in this seed set were silently eaten until 2026-08-21. Only `components.objects` is scanned, so seed never moves to a top-level `objects` key. Enforced by `npm run check:seed-refs` (tests/validate-seed-refs.js).

objects._note: humaniq-hours-process-redesign (tasks.md 5.1): TimeEntry seeds linked to the seeded timesheets by real timesheetId slug links. The register seed import runs through the ordinary ObjectCreatingEvent pipeline, so the stamping listeners DO fire on it: TimesheetProcessStampListener forces every created Timesheet to status draft with nulled process fields (measured on CI run 32504408914 — the seeded statuses below do NOT survive import). tests/e2e/ci-seed.sh therefore walks the three 2026-05 timesheets through their real lifecycle edges after import; the status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason literals below document the TARGET states and feed that walk (the rejectionReason text is read from here). Every listener-owned value (hours, userId, costCenter, administrationId, the per-entry allocation copies) is carried as a literal CONSISTENT with what the listeners derive: hours = (endedAt - startedAt - breakMinutes)/60, the entries of one timesheet sum exactly to its seeded hours, share its projectId/costCenter/billable (the homogeneous-aggregate contract, REQ-TEC-003/004), and userId mirrors the linked Employee's nextcloudUserId (absent where the employee link does not resolve — devries/bakker, the fail-closed K=2 rows).
